- The slipway: two long parallel timber rails running from the foreground down into the calm water of the cove.
- The scaffold: one wide timber plank resting on two sturdy timber trestles standing on the slipway against the hull's side.
- The stack of iron plates: a neat stack of curved dark iron hull plates on a low timber pallet, hip-high to the person.
- The brazier: a small round iron brazier on exactly three iron legs, each standing on the timbers, a bed of glowing coals in it.
- The bellows: one pair of small wooden hand bellows with a leather body and a short brass nozzle aimed at the coals, held by the heater's two mittens.
- The hammer: a small brass riveting hammer with a wooden handle, held by the riveter's two mittens.
- The rope coil: one thick hemp rope coiled flat on the timbers.

## Setting
A hidden cove on a volcanic island: smooth dark basalt cliffs curve round the slipway on both sides, a natural sea arch opens in the far cliff onto the calm open sea and the dawn sky, and the water inside the cove is still and clear turquoise. The air is still.

## Light
Soft warm dawn light through the sea arch from behind the hull is the key light, with warm rim light on every figure and a gentle warm sheen along the hull's top. The brazier's coals throw a small warm orange glow on the heater, the bellows and Ouro. Soft contact shadows under every foot, the trestles, the plate stack and Ouro's coil. The person's warm inner light glows softly through the glass head.

## Palette
Dawn peach and soft blue, dark basalt, turquoise water, dark iron with warm brass, honey timber; charcoal and cream; emerald for Ouro; amber for the riveter; teal for the heater; one small orange glow of coals.

## Must not
- No third arm, no extra or missing limbs and no fused legs.
- No separate fingers on any hand: mitten hands, exactly one thumb, never separate fingers; no pointing, no waving, no thumbs-up.
- No visible hand on the person.
- No stretched, tall-and-thin or stick-figure person; no green, mint, milky or coloured-balloon person; no face and no ears on the person; no hat on the person.
- No text, letters, numbers, logos or symbols anywhere.
- No emoji faces on visors: no ">" or "<" eyes, no tongues, no winks, no mouths, no grins, no curved line under the eyes.
- No comic or cartoon styling: no outlines, no exaggerated squash and stretch.
- No glowing trails or lines of light; no sparks flying.
- No phones, laptops, monitors, screens or power tools.
- No tiles, cells or facets on the glass bodies.
- Not the 1954 film's submarine: no saw-toothed spines along the back, no fins, no big round eye-window at the bow, no crocodile shape, no studs or spikes; and no modern submarine: no conning tower, no periscope, no sail or dive planes.
- No cranes, chains, hooks or ladders.
- No sun disc in the sky, no sunbeams, no lens flare.
- No figure facing the camera full on.
- No giant Ouro: his coil is never taller than the heater's head.
- No tongs, rods, wires or loose sticks; every bar and leg ends on something it is attached to.
- No image fades or vignettes.

## Output
Three candidates, each generated whole at 1536x1024, quality high. The chosen one ships whole as a 3:2 picture beside the chapter's title, and as an 8:3 band cut from rows 224 to 800 on phones. The night twin is a relight of the chosen picture: the same frame, figures and poses under a starry night sky, lit by the brazier's coals and the moon through the sea arch.

Seen from inside the Nautilus through the thick glass of a round porthole, a giant squid clings to the hull, two of its arms spread across the glass and one huge, curious eye peering in.

- What: a giant squid of Jules Verne's novel holding fast to the submarine's hull, curious and gentle, never menacing.

- Outfit: none.
- Expression: curious and calm: its one huge round eye wide and glistening, looking in at us, a soft highlight on its dark pupil.

- Limbs: exactly two arms visible on the glass, each coming from behind its head and tapering to a soft rounded tip near the frame's lower edge; no other arm and no tentacle anywhere in the frame.
- Hands: none: each arm's underside rests on the glass, its suckers pressed flat to it.
- Facing: its eye faces the camera through the glass; its body runs away from us into the sea.

The open sea a little way below the surface, around the hull of Jules Verne's Nautilus: deep, clear blue-green water with soft shafts of light from far above, a few tiny bubbles and a far-off shoal of small silver fish, quiet and still; the water moves nothing.

Deep blue-green sea, darker teal in the depths, rose and coral for the squid, pale rose suckers, a little silver for the fish.

- No gore, no slime and no gross wet detail.
- No people, robots, snakes or other figures.
- No text, letters, numbers, logos or symbols anywhere.
- No comic or cartoon styling: no outlines, no exaggerated squash and stretch.
- No glowing trails or lines of light.
- No cracks, scratches, drops or fog on the glass.
- No image fades or vignettes.

- What: three small, gentle moon jellyfish.
- Material: soft, translucent, glassy bells, faintly glowing pale blue and violet from within.
- Height: each bell about a tenth of the frame's height.

- Limbs: none; two wide wings and one thin tail.
- Facing: three-quarter view toward the camera, heading to the left.

## Props
- None.

## Setting
Open sea fifty fathoms down: deep, clear blue fading darker below, calm, with drifting marine snow.

## Light
One key light: dim blue daylight from far above, lighting the tops of the jellyfish and the ray's back; the jellyfish glow softly from within.

## Palette
Deep blue and indigo water, pale blue and violet glow, dark blue-grey ray.

## Must not
- No window frame, brass ring, rivets, bolts, wall, ship or submarine.
- No people, robots or other animals.
- No text, letters, numbers, logos or symbols.
- No comic or cartoon styling: no outlines.
- No glowing trails or lines of light, no fog on the glass, no image fades or vignettes.
- No scary creatures: no stingers or long tangled tentacles.
